answer: Each epoch verifiers cut random graph edges and flood a nonce along survivor paths; every vertex must co-sign in one round. Real operators hold disjoint uplinks and still hear it. Sybil names share one upstream wharf, so a cut on that bottleneck silences them together; simultaneous silence is the linkage proof that slashes their bond. In a tundra, too few alternate paths mask that hop. The attacker must rent N independent egresses and clocks each epoch, and one cut burns N names at once, so more shells cannot diversify the risk. Code cannot mint independent failure domains.
